sentence: This project studies how damaged mitochondria and changes in metabolism lead to either fibrosis or emphysema in chronic lung disease caused by cigarette smoke.
This project tries to find out how cells control nucleotide and iron metabolism so that mammalian physiology can respond to changes in these nutrients.
This project studies how a disease-causing mutation in a transcription factor disrupts valve formation and cardiac development, using human stem cell and animal models.
This project compares the latent viral reservoirs of two HIV subtypes and tries to find out how their makeup influences reactivation.
This project studies how synaptic plasticity drives aggression reward and motivation in both sexes, including the roles of glutamate and oxytocin.
This project provides help with statistical analyses, research design, spatial analyses and predictive modeling for researchers, and builds workshops on these tools.
This project uses human adult stem cell-derived neurons to study a protein that plays a key role in chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy.
This project builds imaging ligands to study how DNA damage and altered immune function in the brain relate to Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how the soft coating on cancer cells physically protects them from attack by Natural Killer cells of the immune system.
This project builds methods that use whole-genome sequencing data to study why short tandem repeats in human DNA expand and contract.
This project tries to build community standards for describing environmental exposures and linking them to human health and disease data, focusing on water contamination.
This project uses computer simulations, machine learning and kinetic models to study how elongation factors work during transcription and what goes wrong in human diseases.
This project offers sequencing technologies and services for studying cancer genomics and epigenomics, and plans to expand single-cell and spatial multiomics tools.
This project investigates what causes rearrest during resuscitation after sudden cardiac arrest and how to prevent it.
This project develops, adapts and puts into practice a healthy eating program in the community by working with local churches.
This project builds a vaccine that uses non-integrating lentiviral vectors to make cells produce HIV proteins and trigger lasting immune responses.
This project builds mRNA vaccines that aim to make the body produce antibodies against a conserved region of the HIV envelope protein.
This project tests how to use an immunotherapy injected directly into tumors, alone and with approved immunotherapies, to treat advanced melanoma.
This project studies how the human transporter Sialin works and tries to find a way to rescue Sialin mutations that cause disease.
This project uses single-cell co-culture and gene expression profiling to find T cells that recognize tumor antigens in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
